title: Affine base change for the right adjoint of a proper flat morphism
statement: Let Y and Y' be affine schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let g:Y'\to Y be a morphism, and let f:X\to Y be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and of finite presentation. Form X'=X\times_Y Y' with g_X:X'\to X and f':X'\to Y' [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let a and a' be right adjoints to Rf_* and Rf'_* on quasi-coherent derived categories [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Then for every K in D_QCoh(Y), the canonical base-change morphism Lg_X^*a(K)\to a'(Lg^*K) is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write Y=Spec(A) and Y'=Spec(A'). Since f is flat, O_X[0] is a bounded complex of quasi-coherent modules flat over Y, so [lem-pc-rf-base-change-complex] with G^\bullet=O_X[0] and arbitrary E\in D_QCoh(X) shows that the canonical base-change transformation \beta:Lg^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*Lg_X^* is an isomorphism on D_QCoh(X). Hence the canonical morphism Lg_X^*a(K)\to a'(Lg^*K) of [def-sc-duality-equation-base-change-map] is defined, and the hypothesis of [lem-sc-flat-precompose-pus] holds. Moreover, for x in X over y in Y and y' in Y' over y, O_{X,x} is flat over O_{Y,y}, so Tor_i^{O_{Y,y}}(O_{X,x},O_{Y',y'})=0 for i>0: f and g are Tor independent in the sense of [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hom-out-of-perfect].

source.place: Tag 0AA8 (Lemma 48.6.2), definition of the base-change map and case (1) Tor-independence hypothesis

proof.text: Choose a single perfect generator M of D_QCoh(X) by [lem-pc-perfect-generator-exists]. The morphism g is affine because Y and Y' are affine, so its base change g_X is affine; therefore [lem-pc-perfect-generator-pullback] says that Lg_X^*M generates D_QCoh(X'). Apply [lem-pc-proper-support-perfect-direct-image] with E=M and with G^\bullet=O_X[0]. The latter is finitely presented and flat over Y because f is flat, and its support X is proper over Y because f is proper; hence E\otimes^L G^\bullet\simeq M, so Rf_*M is perfect and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change.

proof.text: Let c:Lg_X^*a(K)\to a'(Lg^*K) be the canonical morphism of Step 1. By [lem-sc-flat-precompose-pus] (its hypotheses hold by Step 1), R\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(Lg_X^*M,c) precomposed with the pullback comparison R\operatorname{Hom}_X(M,a(K))\otimes^{\mathbf L}_AA'\to R\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(Lg_X^*M,Lg_X^*a(K)) equals the composite of the adjunction isomorphism for a [lem-pc-global-hom-adjunction], the algebraic RHom base-change map for Rf_*M, the isomorphism induced by \beta_M^{-1} (Step 1), and the adjunction isomorphism for a' [lem-pc-global-hom-adjunction]. The pullback comparison is an isomorphism by [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hom-out-of-perfect], since M is perfect, a(K)\in D_QCoh(X), and f, g are Tor independent (Step 1). The algebraic RHom base-change map is an isomorphism by [lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect], since Rf_*M is perfect (Step 2, [lem-pc-proper-support-perfect-direct-image]). Hence R\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(Lg_X^*M,c) is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AA8 (Lemma 48.6.2), proof of case (1), adjunction and RHom comparison

proof.text: The cone of the canonical map has zero derived Hom from the generator Lg_X^*M by Step 3. Since that object generates D_QCoh(X'), the cone is zero, so the canonical map Lg_X^*a(K)\to a'(Lg^*K) is an isomorphism. As K was arbitrary, this holds for every K in D_QCoh(Y).
